PREFACE
This Code constitutes a recodification of the general and permanent ordinances of Columbia County, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the 1979 Code, as supplemented through November 16, 1999, and ordinances subsequently adopted by the board of commissioners. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of the 1979 Code, as supplemented, and any subsequent ordinance included herein.
The chapters of the Code have been conveniently arranged in alphabetical order, and the various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage. Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may be included by using one of the reserved chapter numbers. Care should be taken that the alphabetical arrangement of chapters is maintained when including new chapters.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. The following are typical parts of codes of ordinances, which may or may not appear in this Code at this time, and their corresponding prefixes:
LOCAL LAWS | LL:1
LOCAL LAWS COMPARATIVE TABLE | LLCT:1
CODE | CD1:1
CODE APPENDIX | CDA:1
CODE COMPARATIVE TABLES | CCT:1
STATE LAW REFERENCE TABLE | SLT:1
LOCAL LAWS INDEX | LLi:1
CODE INDEX | CDi:1
Indexes
The indexes have been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the indexes themselves which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up-to-date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up-to-date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.
Acknowledgments
This publication was under the direct supervision of Ron K. McLaughlin, Code Attorney, and Leesa Hampton, Editor, of the Municipal Code Corporation, Tallahassee, Florida. Credit is gratefully given to the other members of the publisher's staff for their sincere interest and able assistance throughout the project.
The publisher is most grateful to Phebe Dent, County Clerk for her cooperation and assistance during the progress of the work on this publication. It is hoped that their efforts and those of the publisher have resulted in a Code of Ordinances which will make the active law of the county readily accessible to all citizens and which will be a valuable tool in the day-to-day administration of the county's affairs.

ADOPTING ORDINANCE
ORDINANCE NO. 01-7
AN ORDINANCE OF THE BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS OF COLUMBIA COUNTY, GEORGIA ADOPTING AND ENACTING A NEW CODE OF ORDINANCES FOR COLUMBIA COUNTY, GEORGIA; PROVIDING FOR THE REPEAL OF CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT INCLUDED THEREIN; PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER OF AMENDING SUCH CODE; AND PROVIDING WHEN SUCH CODE AND THIS ORDINANCE SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE.
THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE BOARD, AND IT IS HEREBY ORDAINED BY AUTHORITY OF SAME, AS FOLLOWS:
Section 1. The Code entitled "Code of Ordinances, Columbia County, Georgia," (the "Code") published by Municipal Code Corporation, Part I consisting of Articles I through V and Part II consisting of chapters 1 through 90, each inclusive, is adopted.
Section 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature enacted on or before May 15, 2001, and not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
Section 3. The repeal provided for in section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
Section 4. Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in accordance with the provisions of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
Section 5. Ordinances adopted after May 15, 2001 are incorporated as part of this Code and to the extent that such ordinances amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code, they shall be construed as amending or referring to like provisions of the new Code.
Section 6. This ordinance shall become effective upon its adoption and the Code shall become effective October 1, 2001.
Adopted September 18, 2001.

In the construction of this Code of Ordinances, the following definitions and rules of construction shall be observed, unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the board of commissioners:
Chairman, other officers. Whenever the term "chairman" is used it shall mean the chairman of the board of commissioners of Columbia County. Whenever titles of various officers are used, they shall refer to the persons holding such positions with Columbia County.
Code. The term "Code" shall mean this Code of Ordinances, Columbia County, Georgia.
Commission, board of commissioners, county commission, governing authority, governing body. The terms "commission," "board of commissioners," "county commission," "governing authority" and "governing body" shall each mean the board of commissioners of Columbia County, Georgia.
Computation of time. Except as otherwise provided by time period computations specifically applying to other laws, when a period of time measured in days, weeks, months, years or other measurements of time, except hours, is prescribed for the exercise of any privilege or the discharge of any duty, the first day shall not be counted but the last day shall be counted; and, if the last day falls on Saturday or Sunday, the party having such privilege or duty shall have through the following Monday to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the last day prescribed for such action shall fall on a public or legal holiday as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 1-4-1, the party having the privilege or duty shall have through the next business day to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the period of time prescribed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
County. The term "the county" or "this county" shall mean Columbia County, Georgia.
Day. The term "day" shall mean a calendar day of 24 hours.
Delegation of authority. Whenever a provision appears requiring the division director of the county to do some act or make certain inspections it is to be construed to authorize the division director to designate, delegate and authorize subordinates to perform the required act or make the required inspection unless the terms of the provision or section expressly provide otherwise.
Following. The term "following" shall mean next after.
Gender. A word importing one gender shall extend and be applied to the other genders, if the context so permits.
Interpretation. In the interpretation and application of any provision of this Code, it shall be held to be the minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, convenience and general welfare. Where any provision of the Code imposes greater restrictions upon the subject matter than the general provision imposed by other provisions of this Code, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be deemed to be controlling.
Joint authority. All words giving a joint authority to three or more persons or officers shall be construed as giving such authority to act upon the concurrence of a majority of such persons or officers.
Keeper and proprietor. The terms "keeper" and "proprietor" shall mean and include the persons, firms, associations, corporations, receivers, trustees, personal representatives, clubs and partnerships, whether acting by themselves or through a servant, agent or employee.
Month. The term "month" shall mean a calendar month.
Nontechnical and technical words. Words and phrases shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but technical words and phrases and such others as may have acquired a peculiar and appropriate meaning in law shall be construed and understood according to such meaning.
Number. A word importing the singular number only may extend and be applied to several persons and things as well as to one person and thing.
Oath. The term "oath" shall be construed to include an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath, and in such cases the terms "swear" and "sworn" shall be equivalent to the terms "affirm" and "affirmed."
Or, and. The term "or" may be read "and," and the term "and" may be read "or" if the context requires or permits it.
Owner. The term "owner," applied to a building or land, shall include any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common or tenant in partnership of the whole or of a part of such building or land.
Person. The term "person" shall extend and be applied to associations, clubs, societies, firms, partnerships, limited partnerships, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships and other entities and bodies politic and corporate as well as to individuals.
Personal property. The term "personal property" shall include every species of property except real property, as described in this section.
Preceding. The term "preceding" shall mean next before.
Premises. Whenever the term "premises" is used it shall mean place or places.
Property. The term "property" shall include real and personal property.
Public place. The term "public place" shall mean any park, cemetery, schoolyard or open space adjacent thereto, or any area available and/or accessible to the public, regardless of whether privately or publicly owned.
Real property. The term "real property" shall include lands, buildings, tenements, hereditaments, whatever is growing upon or affixed to land, and rights issuing out of, annexed to and exercisable within or about land.
Residence. The term "residence" shall be construed to mean the place adopted by a person as his place of habitation, and to which, whenever he is absent, he has the intention of returning. When a person eats at one place and sleeps at another, the place where such person sleeps shall be deemed his residence.
Schedule of fees and charges. The term "schedule of fees and charges" shall mean the official consolidated list maintained in the county clerk's office which lists rates for utility or other public enterprises, fees of any nature, deposit amounts and various charges as determined from time to time by the board of commissioners.
Seal. The term "seal" shall mean the county seal or the seal of the corporation.
Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" shall mean any portion of a street between the curbline and the adjacent property line intended for the use of pedestrians, excluding parkways.
Signature or subscription. The "signature" or "subscription" of a person shall include a mark when the person cannot write.
State. The term "state" or "the state" shall mean the State of Georgia.
Street. The term "street" shall be construed to embrace streets, avenues, boulevards, roads, alleys, lanes, viaducts and all other public highways in the county.
Tenant, occupant. The term "tenant" or "occupant," applied to a building or land, shall include any person holding a written or oral lease or who occupies the whole or a part of such building or land, either alone or with others.
Time. Words used in the past or present tense include the future as well as the past and present.
Week. The term "week" shall be construed to mean a calendar week of seven days.
Written or in writing. The term "written" or "in writing" shall be construed to include any representation of words, letters or figures, whether by printing or otherwise.
Year. The term "year" shall mean a calendar year unless some other beginning and ending dates are specified.
(Code 1979, § 2-1-2; Ord. No. 99-15, § 2-1-2, 12-16-1999)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all drinks or beverages containing alcohol, including, but not limited to, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Alcoholic treatment facility means any alcohol treatment facility owned and operated by the state or county, including the buildings and the surrounding property or campus directly incorporated into such use.
Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume, and including but not limited to ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small/low-alcohol beer and strong beer. The terms do not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Board of commissioners means the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County.
Church building means the main structure used by any religious organization for purposes of worship and the surrounding property or campus directly incorporated into such use in compliance with the zoning ordinances of the county.
County park or playground means a park, recreation center, ball fields or playgrounds owned and operated by the county for use by the citizens of the county.
Distilled spirits or spirituous liquor means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Eating establishment means a business establishment which sells prepared food for consumption on the premises, with a full service kitchen offering food service every hour such establishment is open, and deriving at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared food items which shall not include the sale of any alcoholic beverages. An eating establishment which was in operation on January 1, 1992, possessed a county business license at that time, and has been in continuous operation since January 1, 1992, must have its full service kitchen approved by the health department and the development services division. Any other eating establishment must have its full service kitchen approved by the health department, development services division and the fire marshal where state law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage made from fruits, berries or grapes, containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Full service kitchen means a kitchen that must contain at least a three-compartment pot sink, a commercial grade stove or grill and oven which is permanently installed, and a commercial grade cooler or refrigerator. The full service kitchen must be approved by the health department, development services division, and the fire marshal, where State law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Governing authority means the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County.
Growler means a glass bottle not to exceed 64 ounces that is filled by a licensee or employee of the licensed establishment with beer from a keg.
Hotel means a business establishment, which provides sleeping accommodations for rent, either on a transient or permanent residence basis, either maintaining a minimum of 50 rooms available for rent and having one or more dining rooms with kitchen facilities as required for an eating establishment, or maintaining less than 50 rooms, but at least three rooms which are available for rent, having at least one dining room with kitchen facilities as required for an eating establishment, and deriving gross sales from the sale of prepared food items in an amount exceeding its gross sales from the sale of alcoholic beverages. License means a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages issued pursuant to the terms of this chapter.
Licensee means the person to whom a license under this chapter is issued.
Liter means the metric measurement of volume currently used by the United States.

(a) Citizenship; residency. A license will be issued only to a person who is a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the United States. (1) Where the applicant for a license is an entity other than a natural person, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the entity and an officer having authority to bind the entity. Said entity shall be registered to do business in the State of Georgia.
(2) Licenses issued to entities must be issued jointly to the entity and all of the other persons required by this section to join in the application. All respective partners, officers, directors, or members, as applicable, shall be responsible for the actions of the named licensee and the conduct of the licensed business.
(b) Operation of business. If none of the applicants required above have primary responsibility of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought, then the operating manager shall join in the application. All persons named on the application shall be deemed "applicants".
(c) Background check. The person who has the primary responsibilities of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought shall submit a personnel statement in the form prescribed by the director of development services, and submit to a background check.
(d) Moral character; criminal record. No person or entity shall be granted an alcoholic beverage license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the commission that such persons or partners in the firms or officers and directors of the company shall be of good moral character.
(e) Age. An applicant must be 21 years of age or older.
(f) Interest in business; involvement in business. An applicant must have a bona-fide interest in the business for which the license is sought.
(g) Eligibility. The following individuals are not eligible for an alcoholic beverage license, even if they possess all of the qualifications listed herein.
(1) Any person convicted of a felony within the ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(2) Any person convicted of a misdemeanor within the five years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application
(3) Any person who has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude or gambling within ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(4) Any person whose license to sell alcoholic beverages has been revoked for cause in any county, municipality, state or territory of the United States within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(5) Any person who has knowingly falsified information or made any material misrepresentation on the application for a license under this chapter or any application under the predecessor ordinance for Columbia County submitted within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(6) Any person who has been convicted of a violation of any federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, or sale of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(7) Should any such applicant, partner or officer or director of any applicant entity, after a license has been granted, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of controlled substances, imitation controlled substances, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, said license shall be subject after hearing to immediate suspension or revocation. Should the operating manager be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of narcotics, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, the licensee shall have seven days to report to the director of development services and any such violation 45 days from such conviction to revise its license to add a new operating manager. Failure to report a violation within the time prescribed shall automatically revoke applicant's license.

The board of commissioners or its designated committee may decline to issue a license under this article when any person having any ownership interest in or any control over the land or building in which the establishment to be operated pursuant to the license will be located, or where any person who has control over the operation of the establishment, does not meet the same character requirements as set forth in this section for the licensee.

Applicant must appoint and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this article may be served. The registered agent must be a resident of the county. The licensee shall file the name of such registered agent, along with the written consent to serve of such agent, with the director of development services.

Notwithstanding anything in this division to the contrary, this section shall not prohibit the sale on the premises of any retail consumption dealer of state lottery tickets, cards or games which are legally sold under the laws of the state.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
369:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a retail consumption dealer in a patio/open area type environment on the premises if the retail consumption dealer has been approved to do so by the director of development services.
(b) To obtain such approval, the patio/open area must be enclosed by a permanent structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main structure on the premises covered by the license.

(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
370:
(a) Except for the area and circumstances specified in subsection (c), below, and as specified in section 6-117, no person shall leave the building in which alcoholic beverages are sold with open alcoholic beverage containers unless such person is in a patio/open sales area which is approved in accordance with section 6-89 or on the premises of outdoor commercial recreational establishments with an existing license. 385:
Functions held in the unincorporated area of Columbia County at which alcoholic beverages are sold or provided will require temporary permits except as set out in subsection (4) below.
(1) Temporary permit required. A temporary permit must be purchased for any function at which alcoholic beverages are sold to the guests directly or indirectly. The individuals, or an officer with authority to bind the entity, putting on the function must apply for the temporary permit. In the alternative, if a Columbia County properly licensed retail consumption dealer or a properly licensed retail consumption dealer in another Georgia County that borders on Columbia County is catering the alcoholic beverages being provided at the off-premises function, the temporary permit may be issued to such retail consumption dealer.
(2) Obtaining temporary permit. To obtain a temporary permit, the appropriate person must obtain from Columbia County the necessary application forms and then file with the county, at least 21 days prior to the date of the function, a completed application and pay to the county the required fees. A temporary permit will be good for a period of not more than two days. Prior to the issuance of a temporary permit, the application filed must be approved by the county administrator and the director of the county division that handles the issuance of alcohol licenses. No public notice of the application shall be required for any temporary permit. Alcoholic beverages may be included in the price of admission to the function and no excise taxes shall be paid or collected on such sales. If the temporary permit is being issued to a retail consumption dealer, the dealer must present a copy of its county retail consumption dealer license and any State of Georgia Alcohol Licenses that may be required.
(3) Functions held by licensed retail consumption dealer. Any properly licensed Columbia County retail consumption dealer may obtain a temporary permit for a function which is not held on the premises covered by such dealers license and which may be held outdoors and/or under a tent. To obtain such a temporary permit, the retail consumption dealer must meet all of the requirements in subsections (1) and (2) directly above.
(4) Functions not requiring temporary permit. A temporary permit shall not be required for serving alcoholic beverages when the function is by invitation only, there is no charge made or other consideration provided for the invitation to the function, for admission to the function or for any food or beverages served at the function and the alcoholic beverages have been legally purchased. Such functions include weddings, company banquets, retirement parties, and private church, club or organization events.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
386:
Retail sales of distilled spirits in packages for consumption off the premises shall be made only in establishments dedicated primarily to the retail sale of distilled spirits, beer and/or wine in packages, and located in zoning districts in which such establishments are permitted as a conforming use.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 22-02, § 1(Exh. A), 5-17-2022)
388:

389:
No sales of distilled spirits in packages shall be made except in fully sealed containers. Single sealed cans or bottles or other containers or packages of distilled spirits may be sold.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
390:
(a) Retail sales of beer and/or wine in packages for consumption off the premises shall be made only in establishments maintaining 50 percent of the floor space and storage area in a manner which is devoted principally to the retail sale of other products such as grocery stores, convenience stores, delicatessens and similar type facilities, or in establishments dedicated primarily to the sale of beer and/or wine and/or distilled spirits in packages. Any such establishment must be located in a zoning district in which such establishment is permitted as a conforming use unless the establishment was previously existing establishment qualifying as a nonconforming use.
(b) Retail sales of growlers in compliance with this section shall be authorized for establishments defined in subsection 6-110(a) authorized to sell alcoholic beverages, excluding distilled spirits, by the package. Before making any such retail sales, the holder of the alcohol license for the premises must obtain from Columbia County a permit for the sale of growler's and for providing samples of tap beers pursuant to such regulations as are established by the board of commissioners of the county. However, samples of tap beers may be made available, but shall not exceed more than one ounce nor shall any one individual be offered more than three samples within a 24-hour period.

392:

393:
No sales of beer or wine in packages shall be made, except in full sealed containers. Single cans or bottles or other containers or packages of beer or wine may be sold.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
394:
(a) No retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer shall purchase any alcoholic beverage from any person other than a wholesaler. No wholesaler shall sell any alcoholic beverage to any person other than a retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer; provided, however, that this section shall not prohibit the purchase by one retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer of another retail consumption dealer's or retail package dealer's entire stock in a bona fide purchase of an ongoing business.
(b) No alcoholic beverage shall be delivered to any retail sales outlet in the county, except by a wholesaler. The name of the wholesaler shall be clearly marked on the delivery vehicle.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
396:
(a) Definition. As used in this section, "in-room service" means the delivery of alcoholic beverages as defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-9-10.
(b) License. A hotel, if it has a license to sell alcoholic beverages either by the package and/or by the drink, may be authorized by the board of commissioners to make similar sales through in-room service. A hotel, prior to providing in-room service, must obtain from the county a license permitting such hotel to provide in-room service of alcoholic beverages.
(c) Restrictions and limitations. The sale of alcoholic beverages by in-room service shall be subject to all restrictions and limitations of this chapter relative to the retail sale of alcoholic beverages, except as provided otherwise in this section, and shall be authorized only on such days and during such hours as the sale of the alcoholic beverages in question is otherwise authorized in the county.
(d) Package size. Distilled spirits sold through in-room service shall not be sold in packages containing less than 200 milliliters each.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
397:
Anything in this chapter to the contrary notwithstanding, the board of commissioners may permit the consumption and sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink on the premises of facilities owned by Columbia County, including but not limited to Savannah Rapids Pavilion, Bessie Thomas Community Center, Eubanks-Blanchard Community Center, the Library/Performing Arts Center, Memorial Gardens Complex, Wildwood Park, Exhibition Center and Evans Towne Center Park shall be permitted under the conditions set out in section 6-105 temporary event permits of the Code.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
398:
Wine or beer tastings may be conducted at retail package outlets licensed to sell wine and beer, but not distilled spirits, subject to the following restrictions:
The applicant for a wine or beer tasting permit must hold a valid package license for sale of wine and beer in the state. All wines used for tasting purposes must have been purchased from a licensed state wine wholesaler. Wine bottles or beer containers shall be opened only by the holder of the valid package license and the wine or beer tasting permit or an employee thereof, and samples shall only be poured by such licensee/permittee or an employee thereof. Wine or beer tastings shall be offered not more than once per day and shall not exceed more than two hours. Holders of a wine or beer tasting permit shall not charge for samples or tastings, but may accept donations for a charitable organization located in Columbia County. Wine or beer sampling and tasting is only permitted within the enclosed portion of the premises. Wine or beer tastings must comply with all laws and regulations otherwise pertaining to the sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages in the state. All licensees and permit holders must comply with all applicable state statutes and sections of this Code concerning alcoholic beverages, including but not limited to those dealing with hours of operation, zoning, and distance requirements.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)

401:
Every purchaser at retail of distilled spirits by the drink in the county shall pay a tax thereon at the rate of three percent of the retail price or charge for such drink, or at such higher rate as may be permitted by the laws of the state. Such tax shall not apply in any portion of the county in which an excise tax on the sale of distilled spirits by the drink is being imposed, levied and collected by a municipality. Such tax shall be collected by the retail consumption dealer, who shall remit such tax to the director of development services on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the retail consumption dealer's gross sales derived from the sale of distilled spirits by the drink during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director. Credit card sales shall be reported as part of gross sales, and taxes collected on such credit card sales shall be submitted to the county in the same manner as required for cash sales. Each retail consumption dealer shall be allowed a deduction equal to the rate authorized for deductions from state tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-50, as amended from time to time, provided that such tax is not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 2, 11-1-2016)
402:
There is levied an excise tax computed at the rate of $0.22 per liter, including a proportionate amount calculated at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter, on all sales of distilled spirits and wine in the county by wholesalers to retail consumption dealers and retail package dealers. Such tax shall be paid to the director of development services by the wholesaler selling such distilled spirits or wine to any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the wholesaler's gross sales of distilled spirits and wine in the county during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director. Wine containing less than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume shall not be subject to such tax. It shall be a violation of this chapter for any wholesaler to sell, ship or deliver, in any manner, any distilled spirits or wine to a retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer without collecting such tax. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this chapter for any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer to possess, own, hold, store, display or sell any distilled spirits or wine on which such tax has not been paid. (Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 2, 11-1-2016)
403:
There is levied an excise tax on all beer sold by wholesalers to retail consumption dealers and retail package dealers in the county at the highest rate allowed by the state, but not less than the following:
(1) Where beer is sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons, and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons; and
(2) Where beer is sold in bottles, cans or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of $0.05 per 12 ounces, and a proportionate rate on all fractional parts of 12 ounces.

Such tax shall be paid to the director of development services by the wholesaler selling the beer to any retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer on or before the twentieth day of the following calendar month, along with a report of the wholesaler's gross sales of beer in the county during the reporting period on forms prescribed by the director.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 2, 11-1-2016)
404:
Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the director of development services is not satisfied with the return of the tax or the amount of the tax to be paid to the county by any person, the director may cause an audit of the books and records of the licensee to be performed and may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within the director's possession or that may come into the director's possession. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for one or more monthly periods. It shall be the duty of each licensee subject to the collection or payment of any of the excise taxes set forth in this article to keep and preserve his records relative to the collection and payment of such taxes for three years.
(1) Interest. The amount of the deficiency determination, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the twentieth day after the close of the monthly period in which the amount or any portion thereof should have been returned until the date of payment thereof.
(2) Offsetting of overpayments. In making a deficiency determination, the director may offset overpayments for a period against underpayments for another period, penalties and the interest on underpayments.
(3) Penalty for negligence or disregard of rules and regulations. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to negligence or disregard of rules and regulations, a penalty of 15 percent of the amount of such deficiency shall be added to the tax.
(4) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination is made is due to fraud or an intent to evade any provision of sections 6-151—6-156, or other authorized rules and regulations, a penalty of 25 percent of the deficiency shall be added to such tax.
(5) Notice of director's determination; service of. The director or his designated representative shall give to the licensee written notice of a deficiency determination. The notice may be served personally or by mail. If such service is made by mail, such service shall be made pursuant to section 6-63.
(6) Time within which notice is to be mailed. Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade the provisions of this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the twentieth day of every month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 2, 11-1-2016)
405:
(a) Estimate of gross receipts. If any licensee fails to make a return, the director of development services shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the licensee or of the total sales in the county which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period in respect to which the licensee failed to make the return and shall be based upon any information which is in or may come into the possession of the director. Upon the basis of such estimate, the director shall compute and determine the amount required to be paid to the county, adding to such determined sum a penalty equal to 15 percent thereof. One or more determinations may be made for one or more periods.
(b) Offsetting of overpayments. If making a determination, the director may offset overpayments for a period or penalties against the interest on the underpayments.
(c) Interest on amount found due. The amount of the determination, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the twentieth day of the month following the monthly period for which the amount, or any portion thereof, should have been returned, until the date of payment.
(d) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. If the failure of any person to file a return is due to fraud or an intent to evade sections 6-151—6-156 or rules and regulations, a penalty of 25 percent of the amount required to be paid by the person, exclusive of penalties, shall be added thereto in addition to the 15 percent penalty provided in section 6-154(d).
(e) Giving of notice; manner of service. Promptly after making his determination, the director shall give to the person written notice, to be served personally or by mail in the manner prescribed for service of notice in section 6-63.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 2, 11-1-2016)
406:
(a) Security. Whenever the director of development services deems it necessary to ensure compliance with sections 6-151—6-156, he may require any person subject to such sections to deposit with him such security as the director may determine. The amount of the security shall be fixed by the director, but shall not be greater than twice the person's estimated average liability for the period for which he files returns, determined in such a manner as the director deems proper, or $10,000.00, whichever amount is the lesser. The amount of the security may be increased by the director subject to the limitations provided in this section. The director may sell the security at public auction, with the approval of the board of commissioners, if it becomes necessary to do so in order to recover any tax or any amount required to be collected, interest or penalty due. Notice of the sale may be served upon the person who deposited the security personally or by mail. If service is by mail, it shall be made in the manner prescribed for service of a notice of determined deficiency and shall be addressed to the person at his address as it appears in the records of the director. Upon any sale, any surplus above the amounts due shall be returned to the person who deposited the security.
(b) Notice of delinquency to persons holding credits or property of delinquent; duty of persons so notified. If any person is delinquent in the payment of the amount required to be paid by him, or if a delinquency determination has been made against him which remains unpaid, the director may, not later than three years after the payment became delinquent, give notice thereof by registered mail to all persons in the county having in their possession or under their control any credits or other personal property belonging to the delinquent, or owing any debts to the delinquent. After receiving the notice, the persons so notified shall neither transfer nor make any other disposition of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession or under their control at the time they receive the notice until the director consents to a transfer or disposition, or until 20 days elapse after the receipt of the notice. All persons so notified shall, within five days after receipt of the notice, advise the director of all of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession, under their control or owing by them.
(c) Action for tax collection. At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article becomes due and payable, and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article, the director may bring an action in the courts of this state, any other state or of the United States in the name of county to collect the amount delinquent, together with penalties and interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(d) Duty of successors or assignees of licensee to withhold tax from purchase money. If any licensee liable for any amount under sections 6-151—6-156 sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold a sufficient amount of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the director showing that he has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(e) Liability for failure to withhold; certificate of notice of amount due; time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold the purchase price as required, he becomes personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price valued in money. Within 30 days after receiving a written request from the purchaser for a certificate, the director shall either issue the certificate or mail notice to the purchaser at his address, as it appears on the records of the director, of the amount that must be paid as a condition of issuing the certificate. The time within which the obligation of the successor may be enforced shall begin at the time the licensee sells out his business or at the time that the determination against the licensee becomes final, whichever occurs later.
(f) Refund of tax, penalty or interest paid more than once or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax, penalty or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the county under sections 6-151—6-156, it may be offset as provided in subsection 6-154(c) or it may be refunded provided a verified claim in writing therefor, stating the specific grounds upon which the claim is founded, is filed with the director within three years from the date of payment. The claim shall be audited and shall be made on forms provided by the director. If the claim is approved by the director and the board of commissioners, the excess amount collected or paid may be refunded or may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person from whom it was collected or by whom paid, and the balance may be refunded to such person, his administrators or executors.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)

410:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned animal means any animal which has been left unattended or uncared for on public or private property.
Advisory board means the animal services advisory board created under this article.
Animal means any member of the kingdom Animalia.
Animal services department means the animal services department within the community and leisure services division of the Columbia County Government.
Animal control officer means any employee of the county or the county sheriff, duly commissioned under the legal authority of the county to enforce the rules and regulations of this chapter. This position shall also be referred to as "dog control officer" as referenced in O.C.G.A. tit. 4, ch. 8.
Animal shelter means any facility operated by or under contract for the county for the purpose of impounding or harboring seized, stray, homeless, abandoned or unwanted dogs, cats and other animals.
Animal running at-large means any animal not under immediate control, which is not on a leash, not in a vehicle or not confined within the property limits of his owner, but shall not include animals which are actively engaged in sporting activities, including, but not limited to, hunting, field trials, shows, competition or other exhibitions.
Authority means the Columbia County Probate Court, as deemed the hearing board for dangerous and vicious dog appeals.
Cat means any animal classified as Felis domestica.
Cruel tethering means to tether an animal in a manner that:
(1) Causes injury or illness;
(2) Utilizes a tether that is too short for an unattended animal or for the animal to urinate or defecate in a separate area from there area where it must eat, drink, or lie down; or
(3) Does not permit the animal access to adequate food, water, shade, or shelter.
County kennel means any premises designated by the animal care and control division for the purpose of impounding and caring for dogs, cats and other animals found running at-large in violation of this chapter.

State of emergency is as defined by O.C.G.A. § 38-3-3(5), and means a condition declared by the governor when, in his judgment, the threat or actual occurrence of a disaster, emergency or energy emergency is of sufficient severity and magnitude as to warrant extraordinary efforts in preventing or alleviating the damage, loss, hardship or suffering threatened or caused thereby.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-2(3)(b))
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
782:
The health, safety and welfare of the citizens and property of the county may be jeopardized during an emergency, disaster or the subsequent recovery period by the inability of the board of commissioners to act expediently without regard to certain formalities. The board of commissioners is authorized pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 38-3-27(b) and 38-3-28 to take actions necessary to provide for the health and safety of persons and property during periods of emergency or disaster, provided that such actions are not inconsistent with any orders, rules or regulations promulgated by the governor of the state or his delegate. The powers and functions exercised by the board of commissioners necessary to conduct the business and affairs of the county during an emergency or disaster proclaimed as such by the appropriate state official may continue without regard to compliance with time consuming procedures and formalities pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 38-3-54. In accordance with O.C.G.A. §§ 36-10-4(c)(5) and 32-4-63(6), certain formalities concerning public works contracts may be waived when necessitated by an emergency. The board of commissioners believes that it is desirable to have legislation in place authorizing the board of commissioners to waive certain formalities and procedures, as necessary, in case of an emergency, natural disaster or the subsequent recovery period.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(1))
783:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Fee means any fee or rate charged by the county for building permits, land disturbance permits, zoning applications, special land use permits, temporary land use permits and other fees relating to the reconstruction, repair and clean up of areas impacted by a disaster or emergency. This term shall not include those fees collected by the county on behalf of the federal or state government, or those fees charged by the county pursuant to a federal or state statute or regulation.
Subsequent recovery period means the period of time that a disaster or emergency continues to cause disruptions in the area impacted by the disaster or emergency, which period of time shall not exceed six months after the state of emergency declaration by the governor is terminated unless extended by official action of the board of commissioners.
Temporary dwelling means any mobile or easily movable home, trailer, recreational vehicle or structure not otherwise permitted by the zoning regulations in a particular zoning district.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(3)(a), (c), (d))
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.

Upon proclamation by the appropriate state official of an emergency or disaster of manmade or natural causes or enemy attack impending on or affecting the state or the United States, the affairs and business of the county may be conducted at places other than the regular or usual place thereof, within or outside of the county, when it is not prudent, expedient or possible to conduct business at the regular location. When such meetings occur outside of the county, all actions taken by the board of commissioners shall be as valid and binding as if performed within the county. Such meetings may be called by the presiding officer or any two members of the board of commissioners without regard to or compliance with time consuming procedures and formalities otherwise required by law.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(2)(a))
785:
Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the appropriate state official, or upon the determination by the board of commissioners or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the board of commissioners, its designee or the emergency interim successor may contract for public works without letting such contract out to the lowest, responsible bidder, and without advertising and posting notification of such contract for four weeks; provided, however, that any public works contract entered into pursuant to this section shall be entered on the minutes of the board of commissioners as soon as practical, and the nature of the emergency described therein.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(2)(b))

Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the appropriate state official, or upon the determination by the board of commissioners or its designee, of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the board of commissioners, its designee or the emergency interim successor may temporarily suspend the enforcement of this Code, or any portion thereof, where:
(1) The emergency or disaster is of such a nature that immediate action outside this Code is required;
(2) Such suspension is consistent with the protection of the public health, safety and welfare; and
(3) Such suspension is not inconsistent with any federal or state statutes or regulations.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(2)(c))
787:

(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(2)(d))

The temporary permit shall not exceed six months in duration. In the case of continuing hardship and in the discretion of the board of commissioners or its designee, the permit may be extended for an additional period of six months. Upon expiration of the temporary permit or an extension, the temporary dwelling shall be removed.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-1(2)(e))

The health, safety and welfare of the people and property in the county may be jeopardized during an emergency, disaster or imminent threat thereof, by the presence of looters, vandals, thieves and others who would take advantage of the confusion and devastation that accompanies such an event. The board of commissioners is authorized pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 38-3-27(b)(2) and 38-3-28 to take any action necessary to provide for the health and safety of persons and property during periods of emergency or disaster, provided that such actions are not inconsistent with any orders, rules or regulations promulgated by the governor or his delegate. The board of commissioners believes that it is desirable to have legislation in place authorizing the board of commissioners to enact a curfew when it is determined necessary to maintain order and to protect either the people or property during an emergency or disaster in all or certain areas of the county.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-2(1))

The resolution may, in the discretion of the board of commissioners, also exempt regular employees of local industries traveling to and from their jobs with appropriate identification, news media employees, building and repair contractors, properly registered according to section 30-113, performing activities related to construction, repair, renovation or improvement of buildings and other structures damaged during the disaster or emergency.
(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-2(3)(a), (b))

793:
(a) Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor or other appropriate state official, or upon the determination by the board of commissioners or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the board of commissioners, its designee or the emergency interim successor may adopt a resolution instituting a curfew when it is determined necessary to protect and safeguard the people and property in the county.
(b) All unincorporated areas of the county shall be subject to the terms of the curfew, unless otherwise specified in the resolution.

(Code 1979, § 2-5.7-2(4))

(a) Intent. The intent of this section is to provide guidance for the responsible design and development of land, while allowing the flexibility to develop sites with unique topographical or design features that require more extensive grading than a typical development.
(b) Purpose. The purpose of this section is to:
(1) Allow for development of planned developments with creative and imaginative design features that are compatible with the area, but that may require more extensive grading than a typical development;
(2) Ensure that the development of land maintains consistency with the county's comprehensive plan and all subsequent amendments and updates;
(3) Protect the character and integrity of development within the county;
(4) Provide for the effective development of public facilities and services for the site; and
(5) Encourage efficient use of land for preservation of sensitive environmental and cultural resources, such as open space areas, waterways, wetlands, and topographic features.
(c) Applicability. This section shall apply to all land disturbing activity beyond the minimum necessary to construct roads and related structures, best management practices for managing stormwater, stock pile staging areas, and material storage areas. Land disturbing activity required to construct individual residential or nonresidential buildings on individual building lots, as well as land disturbing activity required to construct nonresidential or multi-family developments, is exempt from the requirements of this section.
(d) Design requirements.
(1) For sites intended for residential development, a natural, undisturbed buffer with a minimum width of 25 feet shall be maintained along the exterior boundary of a site affected by major site grading. Effective protective measures shall be employed to ensure that the buffer remains undisturbed during construction. Said buffer shall be fully contained in the development's common area. For sites smaller than ten acres, buffer requirements shall follow those required by section 90-139 of this Code. An alternate buffer plan, including the use of a planted berm, for boundaries adjacent to rights-of-way may be approved by the planning commission as part of preliminary plat approval, provided that the alternate plan does not eliminate the undisturbed buffer completely and meets the intent of the overall buffering requirements of this section.
(2) In addition to the requirements of section 90-141 pertaining to tree protection, street trees shall be provided and maintained within, or adjacent to, all existing and proposed street rights-of-way in accordance with the requirements of subsections 90-140(e)(1) through (3) pertaining to street trees.
(3) A geotechnical/soils report prepared by a qualified geotechnical engineer shall be submitted with an application for a land disturbance permit and shall include the following information:
a. Site conditions, including site topography, and vegetation;
b. Engineering characteristics of the subsurface material together with laboratory test results to at least 24 inches below proposed grades or to refusal;
c. Depth to groundwater if present within 24 inches of proposed grades;
d. Conclusions as to the adequacy of the soils of the site for the proposed grading and recommendations of any corrective procedures, if required;
e. Foundation and pavement design criteria. Pavement design criteria shall meet a minimum of eight inches of compacted GAB, two inches of compacted asphalt binder course, and one and one-half inches of compacted surface course; and
f. Site drainage and groundwater management recommendations.
(4) Excavation and slope requirements.
a. Subdrains shall be provided under any curb and gutter on public roadways of excavation greater than four feet.
b. When slopes steeper than six horizontal to one vertical (6H:1V) are located on one parcel, the top and/or toe of the slope shall be no closer than one foot plus 50 percent of the height of the slope to an adjacent property line or environmentally sensitive area, but no less than five feet.
c. At the discretion of the county engineer, slopes steeper than 6H:1V may cross parcel lines provided the following guidelines for supplemental drainage systems or courses are applied:
1. Slopes as steep as 5H:1V may be used across parcel lines provided:
i. On-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting on-site shall not exceed 250 linear feet prior to being captured by the roadway, a parcel owned by the homeowners associated, or a closed drainage system.
ii. Off-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting off-site but ending on-site shall not cross subsequent property lines nor exceed 250 linear feet prior to being captured and routed to a pond by opened and/or closed drainage systems.
2. Slopes as steep as 4H:1V may be used across parcel lines provided:
i. On-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting on-site shall not exceed 200 linear feet prior to being captured by the roadway, a parcel owned by the homeowners associated, or a closed drainage system no further away than the immediately adjacent parcel from which the runoff was generated.
ii. Off-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting off-site but ending on-site shall not cross subsequent property lines nor exceed 200 linear feet prior to being captured and routed to a pond by opened and/or closed drainage systems.
3. Slopes as steep as 3H:1V may be used across parcel lines provided:
i. On-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting on-site shall not exceed 150 linear feet prior to being captured by the roadway, a parcel owned by the homeowner's association, or a closed drainage system located on the parcel from which the runoff was generated.
ii. Off-site surface runoff. Runoff courses starting off-site but ending on-site shall not cross subsequent property lines nor exceed 150 linear feet prior to being captured and routed to a pond by opened and/or closed drainage systems.
d. In all cases where stormwater is being directed to and/or through a parcel to be owned by a homeowner's association (HOA), the preliminary plat, final plat, and the HOA bylaws shall clearly identify the HOA as the responsible party for slope repairs should any signs of slope failure occur. The limits of the slope repair by the HOA shall include repair to failing or failed slopes on the HOA parcel and any contiguous portion of failing or failed slope onto private parcels regardless of slope failure point of origin. Repairs shall be completed within a reasonable amount of time but in no case exceeding six calendar months from the time the failure occurred.
e. Slopes shall not be steeper than 3H:1V unless a slope stability report has been approved by the county engineer.
f. Slopes shall not exceed 20 feet in height unless horizontal benches with a minimum width of six feet are installed every ten feet in height. Horizontal benches shall have proper drainage conveyance.
g. All fills greater than ten feet shall be placed, compacted, inspected and tested in accordance with the following provisions. All monitoring and testing shall be performed by a qualified soil testing agency engaged by the developer.
1. Preparation of ground. The existing ground surface shall be prepared to receive fill by removing vegetation, noncomplying fill, and other incompetent material. Where the slope of the existing ground surface is 5H:1V or steeper, the fill shall be supported on level benches cut into competent material. The bench under the toe of a fill on a slope steeper than 5H:1V shall be at least ten feet wide. The area beyond the toe of fill shall be sloped for sheet overflow or have proper drainage conveyance away from toe. When fill is to be placed over a cut, the bench under the toe of fill shall be at least ten feet wide. The cut shall be accepted by Columbia County prior to placing the fill as a suitable foundation for fill.
2. Subdrains shall be provided under all fills placed in natural drainage courses and in other locations where seepage is evident. Such subdrainage systems shall be of a material and design approved by the county. The permittee shall provide periodic monitoring during the process of subdrain installation to conform to the approved plans.
3. Fill material. Tree limbs, stumps, wood chips, and other such organic material shall not be permitted in fills. Soil containing small amounts of roots may be allowed, providing that the roots are in a quantity and distributed in a manner that will not be detrimental to the future use of the site and the use of such material is approved by the county. Asphalt millings or waste may not be used for fill material. No rock or similar irreducible materials with a maximum dimension greater than eight inches shall be buried or placed in fill except as meeting the following requirements:
i. The oversized material shall be placed ten feet or more below finish grade;
ii. A representative of the soil testing agency shall be present while the oversized material is placed and covered;
iii. Reports submitted by the soil testing agency shall acknowledge the placement of the oversized material and whether the work was performed in accordance with his or her recommendations and the approved plans; and
iv. The location of oversized rock dispersal areas shall be shown on the record drawing. Rock or similar irreducible materials less than eight inches in greatest dimension shall be placed in such a manner as to prevent nesting of oversize particles and to assure that all voids are filled with fine-grained materials.
4. The fill shall be spread in a series of loose lifts, each not exceeding eight inches in thickness, and shall be compacted by sheepsfoot roller or other approved method after each layer is spread. The next lift shall not be placed until the compacted lift is tested or authorized by the soil testing agency.
5. The moisture content of the fill material shall be controlled at the time of spreading and compaction to obtain required relative compaction.
6. All fills shall be compacted to a minimum of 95 percent of maximum density as determined by A.S.T.M. D-1557 or other approved testing methods giving equivalent test results. If the required degree of relative compaction cannot be attained on sloped surfaces, the slope shall be over filled and cut back until the compacted inner core is exposed. Field density shall be determined by A.S.T.M. D-1556.
7. A sufficient number of tests shall occur to satisfy the soil testing agency that all requirements have been met. As a minimum, a field density test, as herein provided, shall be taken for each 18 inches of fill, or portion thereof, measured vertically from the lowest point of the area to be filled, and for each 500 cubic yards of fill placed. In addition, in the case of subdivisions, at least one field density test shall be taken on each lot which receives fill. One field density test shall be taken on the slope face for every four feet in elevation of the slope or every 1,000 square feet of slope for each lot.
8. All fills regulated by this section shall be tested for relative compaction by a qualified soil testing agency. A certificate of compliance with the terms of this section and the grading permit, setting forth densities, relative compaction and other soil characteristics shall be prepared and signed by the soil testing agency. A compaction report shall be submitted to and approved by Columbia County before any final approval of the fill is given and before final platting of the subdivision.
h. All filled lots shall be denoted on the final plat, with reference made to the applicable compaction report.
